observations: Photo 0 shows a bare automotive engine assembly (cylinder head, intake manifold, alternator, wiring harness) sitting on a concrete/paved surface outdoors.
Green paint daubs are visible on several engine surfaces, a marking style common on Nigerian used-parts ('tokunbo') engines, but no brand or model lettering is legible.
A person's legs and sandals are visible in the background, suggesting a roadside or yard sale setting.
No VIN plate, engine code stamp, ECU label, or manufacturer badge is readable in the frame.
No spark plugs, turbo, or full wiring loom confirmed present; only partial harness visible.
No video or audio evidence of the engine running.

claims.evidence: No origin marking, import sticker, or Korean-brand badge visible in photo 0; claim rests on seller's word only.

risks.risk: Unknown make/model means price could range from a small sedan engine to a larger SUV engine; this is the single biggest price driver.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code stamp (usually on block near gearbox mount) or any VIN/parts tag, or a legible manufacturer badge.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this; price list cannot be applied to an unidentified engine type

risks.risk: Running condition unknown (no start-up video, no compression test).
risks.proof: Video of engine cranking/running with sound, or compression test readout.
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-running/for-parts only once identity is established

risks.risk: Completeness unknown - sensors, turbo, injectors, wiring loom may be missing or swapped.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set of the engine including underside and connector ends.
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete/core-only once identity is established

risks.risk: Claimed 'Korean' origin and grade (e.g., direct import vs locally used) cannot be confirmed from a photo.
risks.proof: Photo of import/clearance documentation or a clear origin stamp on the block.
risks.if_unproven: no origin premium applied; treated as unverified local used stock

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/stamp or any identification plate on the block or near the gearbox bell housing.
Photo or video showing the engine starting and running, with audible sound.
Full set of photos from all sides including underside, intake, and exhaust manifold.
Any import/clearance paperwork or origin documentation for the 'Korean parts' claim.
response.reason: The engine's make and model are not legible in the photo, and price for an engine varies enormously by that identity, so even a worst-case price cannot be set until a readable engine code or badge is provided.
